rec.name: Competitor Comparison Table Section
rec.status: Design approved — build status not documented

what.text: A content section that compares your brand with competitors in a feature-by-feature table. The first column is your brand, highlighted as a tall card, and the other columns are named or generic competitors. Each row is one benefit, such as no-code editing, simple integration, support quality or video tutorials. Every cell shows a check or a cross. Your brand gets a check in every row, and competitors miss several. The final design has a headline above the table, for example 'Why do e-com brands choose us?'.

why.text: Shoppers compare options anyway, so the table does it for them in seconds. A column of checks next to red crosses makes the brand's advantages obvious without reading copy. Showing the competitor ticking a few boxes too keeps the comparison credible. Highlighting your own column draws the eye and anchors the brand as the complete option. This reduces risk and clarifies value at the decision point.

how.text: Build a section with a headline, a brand column (logo and name) and 2–3 competitor columns (logo or generic label). Each row is a block with a benefit label plus a check or cross per column. Make the brand column a visually distinct card (dark in the final design, bright green in the variant). Give rows alternating or tinted background bands for readability. Per feedback, check icons in the highlighted column must have strong contrast. The ticket says to make them white so they don't get lost on the dark column, as on the product image. Pick benefits that really differentiate the brand, and keep rows to about 7–8.

items: Rows: benefit label (optional small badge or flag icon)
Per-row, per-column value: check or cross
Highlight column colour (dark or green variant)
Check/cross icon colour and contrast (white checks on the dark column)

dependencies.text: No apps or metafields are stated in the ticket. Assumes static content managed in the theme editor. Needs brand and competitor logo assets and a mobile layout that keeps 3–4 columns legible (not specified in the ticket). Benefit wording must be verified as factually accurate for the brand and competitors.

items: CTA click-through rate after the section
Conversion rate on pages with the section vs. control
Add-to-cart rate (if used on a PDP)

images.caption: Final design: light background, headline, dark highlighted brand column, competitor columns (named brand and 'other providers'), 8 benefit rows with check/cross icons.
Check icons in the dark column were criticised as hard to see; the plan is to make them white.
Dark-theme variant with a bright green highlighted 'We' column and placeholder competitor columns ('Title'). Shows 7 rows of benefits with small check/cross icons.
